author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Silent Failure
challenge.description: A forecast job failed silently for three days, leaving stores ordering blind, and the team never knew until the warehouse was flooded with unsold promotion stock. #reliability_ruth# argues that the performance monitoring must be automated and governed to catch such failures instantly, while #efficiency_emilia# is willing to accept a manual monthly audit of the logs to save on tooling costs.

output.content: I need to be clear about the security posture for the new observability stack. I will not sign off on any modification to the logging infrastructure unless it is fully automated and governed from day one. Manual log reviews or periodic spot checks do not meet our compliance standards for audit trails. If the system cannot prove it is watching itself without human intervention, it is not production ready. This is a hard requirement for my approval. We cannot accept a state where failure detection depends on someone remembering to look at a spreadsheet. The architecture must enforce continuous monitoring before we open the gates for any new data flows.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a non-negotiable line ('hard requirement', 'will not sign off') where crossing it (manual reviews or lack of automation) results in refusal of approval.
